# Contributing to F13 Configurator

Thanks for considering a contribution. This is a small project, the
maintainer reviews everything personally, and the codebase has some
unusual properties — please read this before opening a PR.

## Read this first

Most of this codebase was generated by Claude Code via an automated
[ralph loop](https://github.com/revolutionaryPhoton/f13-configurator-ralph)
driven by a PRD. Human review happens at the diff level, not
line-by-line. There has been no formal security audit. See
[`SECURITY.md`](../SECURITY.md) for the full disclosure.

If you spot something concerning — a parse bug, an injection vector,
a state race — opening an issue is genuinely welcome and useful.

## Repo layout

- `bin/`, `lib/` — shell wizard (Bash 4+, namespaced functions)
- `gui/` — Tauri 2 + Svelte 5 desktop app
- `tests/` — bats tests for the shell side
- `gui/src/**/*.test.ts` — vitest tests for the GUI
- `PRD.md` — product requirements; everything ultimately traces back
  here
- `PROGRESS.md` — story-tracker; the ralph loop reads pending stories
  off this file
- `templates/` — service config templates the wizard renders into
  `generated/`

## Workflow

1. **Open an issue first** for anything larger than a typo. A quick
   sketch of what you'd change and why saves a PR-then-rewrite cycle.
2. **Branch from `main`**. Branch names: `feat/...`, `fix/...`,
   `chore/...`, `docs/...`.
3. **Run the backpressure suite locally** before pushing:
   ```bash
   cd gui && npm run check && npm run test:unit \
     && cargo check --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml
   cd .. && shellcheck -S warning bin/* lib/*.sh && bats tests/
   ```
   CI runs the same suite on every PR (two parallel jobs: macOS for
   the Tauri build + GUI checks, Linux for `shellcheck` + `bats`).
   Both must be green to merge.
4. **Commit convention** (F13 style — enforced loosely; mismatched
   commits get rewritten on squash-merge):
   ```
   <TYPE> [scope]: <description>           (≤ 72 characters)
   ```
   - **TYPE**: `ADD` (new file/feature), `RM` (removal),
     `NF` (new feature), `BF` (bug fix), `RF` (refactor),
     `DOC` (documentation / meta)
   - **scope**: lowercase area, e.g. `[gui]`, `[wizard]`, `[deps]`,
     `[ci]`, `[docs]`, `[repo]`
   - **Only if** an AI coding agent (Claude Code, etc.) actually
     wrote or co-authored the change, end the message with the agent
     **and** the specific model that wrote it:
     ```
     Co-Authored-By: Claude Code, Opus 5
     ```
     Hand-written commits should omit this trailer.
5. **Open a PR**. Link the issue if any, fill in the test plan.
   PRs are squash-merged with a maintainer-rewritten subject in F13
   style.

## What gets accepted

- **Bug fixes**: yes, always — open the PR.
- **Documentation fixes**: yes, always.
- **New features**: discuss in an issue first. Feature scope is
  driven by the PRD; arbitrary feature additions usually don't land
  without prior alignment.
- **Refactors with no behavior change**: usually yes if motivated,
  but coordinate first if the change is broad.

## Code style

- **Shell**: Bash 4+, `set -euo pipefail` on every executed script,
  namespaced functions (`ui::foo`, `ports::pick_free`). Match
  existing patterns in `lib/*.sh`.
- **TypeScript / Svelte**: TS strict mode; Svelte 5 runes
  (`$state`, `$derived`, `$effect`); `biome check` enforces
  formatting; `svelte-check` enforces types.
- **Tests**: every new `.sh` file ships with at least one bats test;
  every new GUI component / store gets at least one vitest test.
  vitest coverage target on TS/Svelte: ≥ 75%.

## Releases

Maintainer cuts releases from `main` following the `CHANGELOG.md`
format (Keep a Changelog). Patch releases (v0.x.Y) happen as
needed; minor releases (v0.X.0) line up with PRD phases.

## Questions

Open an issue or start a discussion. The maintainer answers when
they can — this is a side project.
